headlines: EARLY VOTING ENDS SUNDAY ACROSS MIAMI-DADE AND BROWARD COUNTIES
SOUTH FLORIDA VOTERS PACK THE POLLS BEFORE SUNDAY DEADLINE
MIAMI VOTERS DECIDE THE FUTURE OF VIRGINIA KEY WATERFRONT
draft.article:
South Florida residents are heading to the polls in high numbers as early voting wraps up across Miami-Dade and Broward counties this Sunday at 7 p.m. Voters can cast ballots at any early voting site before Sunday's cutoff, after which voters must go to their assigned precinct on Election Day.

Polling sites like the North Dade Regional Library in Miami Gardens and the Coral Gables branch library have drawn steady crowds, while community members rallied at Charles Hadley Park in Liberty City.

Alongside major political races, City of Miami voters are weighing Referendum 3, a proposal to lease nearly 28 acres of Virginia Key public waterfront for 45 years of redevelopment.

headlines: DEVELOPERS SECURE $220 MILLION LOAN FOR KEY BISCAYNE CONDOS
MASSIVE $220M FINANCING HITS KEY BISCAYNE WATERFRONT
FORMER SILVER SANDS RESORT SET FOR LUXURY REDEVELOPMENT
draft.article: Terra and Fortune International Group secured a $220 million predevelopment loan to construct an oceanfront boutique condominium project on Key Biscayne. The planned development sits on a 4.25-acre parcel at 301 Ocean Drive, previously home to the Silver Sands Beach Resort. The developers purchased the oceanfront site in 2025 for $205 million, marking the largest land transaction in the island history. Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies provided the financing, arranged through Walker and Dunlop. Designed by Touzet Studio and ODP, the project will feature tropical-modern architecture, native landscaping, and green stormwater systems like rain gardens and bioswales. Preconstruction sales will launch before the end of 2026.

headlines: PROSECUTORS DROP FELONY STRANGULATION CHARGE AGAINST RICK ROSS
RICK ROSS CLEARED OF FELONY CHARGE IN MIAMI
STAR ISLAND INCIDENT LEADS TO MISDEMEANOR CHARGE FOR RICK ROSS
draft.article:
Miami prosecutors have dismissed a felony strangulation charge against rapper Rick Ross following an alleged August 28 incident at his Star Island home. Court filings reveal prosecutors cited insufficient evidence, shifting the case to Miami-Dade County Court under a single first-degree misdemeanor charge of domestic violence battery.

The Maybach Music Group founder, whose legal name is William Leonard Roberts II, turned himself in to Miami Beach police on October 1 after a woman reported that an argument over an Instagram post turned physical.

Defense attorney Bradley Horenstein noted photographic evidence showed no signs of neck injury. Ross denies the accusations and calls them fabricated as legal proceedings continue.

draft.article: While South Florida has long set the price ceiling for statewide luxury real estate, high-end western markets are posting historic sales numbers of their own. In Naples, a 15-acre Gulf-front assemblage broke all Florida records with a $225 million transaction, followed by an $86 million sale on Gordon Drive and a recent $70 million closing. Sarasota is also expanding, marked by a $26 million Siesta Key closing in September and a $30.3 million sale last July. Southwest Florida MLS records recorded 73 single-family sales over $10 million in the 12 months ending in August, fueled by wealthy buyers relocating from destinations like Palm Beach and Aspen.

headlines: FLOOD WATCH ISSUED FOR MIAMI-DADE AND BROWARD THROUGH MONDAY
HEAVY RAIN AND FLOOD RISKS HIT SOUTH FLORIDA
COULD UP TO SEVEN INCHES OF RAIN FLOOD MIAMI
draft.article:
The National Weather Service has placed all of Miami-Dade and Broward under a Flood Watch starting Sunday at 10 a.m. through Monday at 3 p.m.

Local neighborhoods face widespread rain and thunderstorms as a weather disturbance lingers near Florida. Rainfall totals could reach between 3 and 5 inches across the region, with isolated pockets seeing 5 to 7 inches.

Breezy conditions will keep rip current risks elevated along local beaches, alongside a High Surf Advisory in Broward. Daily moderate King Tide flooding is expected to ease to minor stages by Tuesday, with drier conditions and mid to upper 80s arriving Wednesday.

headlines: MDC LAUNCHING NEW DENTAL HYGIENE BACHELOR DEGREE IN FALL 2026
MIAMI DADE COLLEGE EXPANDS DENTAL DEGREE PATHWAYS
MDC BECOMES SOUTH FLORIDA'S ONLY PUBLIC DENTAL HYGIENE BACHELOR PROVIDER
draft.article:
Miami Dade College will launch a new Bachelor of Science in Dental Hygiene in Fall 2026, expanding training opportunities right here in our community. The Florida Department of Education approved the 120-credit-hour degree-completion track, making MDC the only public higher education institution in South Florida to provide a full dental hygiene academic pathway.

Designed for working professionals holding an associate degree and an active license, the curriculum covers public health dentistry, clinical research, leadership, and healthcare administration.

Workforce estimates show rising demand for dental professionals in Miami-Dade County through 2032. The new offering helps local hygienists advance their careers affordably while supporting regional oral healthcare needs.

headlines: PELLE LARSSON SHINES AS HEAT BEAT ATLANTA AND INDIANA
HEAT GUARD PELLE LARSSON SURGES ON OFFENSE
WHY HEAT STARS AND COACHES ARE PRAISING SURGING PELLE LARSSON
draft.article:
Pelle Larsson is making a major offensive impact for our Miami Heat following two consecutive victories against Atlanta and Indiana. The versatile wing scored 17 and 18 points across the two games, shooting 11 of 17 from the field while dishing out 11 assists.

During Friday's 145-125 win over Indiana, Larsson shot a perfect 5 for 5 from the floor. Heat coach Erik Spoelstra and center Bam Adebayo both commended his poise and efficiency with the ball in hand. Larsson, who signed a four-year, $60 million contract extension in September, is also holding opponents to 34.7 percent shooting on defense.

Miami now starts a five-game road trip Monday against the Lakers at 10 p.m.

HOW JULIA TUTTLE SECURED 640 MIAMI RIVER ACRES IN 1891
draft.article:
Local history traces back to 1891, the year Julia Tuttle made her move to South Florida. Upon arriving that year, Tuttle completed a major land purchase, buying 640 acres of property situated directly on the north bank of the Miami River.

Julia Tuttle established her presence right along the river with this 640-acre acquisition. Tuttle secured the entire parcel along the north bank during that milestone year of 1891.

Her relocation to South Florida and the purchase along the northern riverbank remain an essential part of our local area's early story.
